name: Anterior tibiofibular ligament
note: Visible from 30° with no help at all. This is what the easy two-thirds looks like.

name: Acromioclavicular ligament
note: Sits on top of the joint line, readable from most angles.

name: Sacrotuberous ligament
note: Large enough to be an easy target; the derived pair is sacrum and hip bone.

name: Anterior cruciate ligament
note: Straight on, nothing removed. The femoral condyles cover it — there is no target here.

name: Anterior cruciate ligament
treatment: femur ghosted, patella and fibula removed
note: The same ligament once the femur is made translucent. This is the treatment the buried third needs.

name: Anterior talofibular ligament
note: Zero percent visible at eleven of twelve angles. The classic sprain ligament is the hardest to show.
